objective: Review commit cb82345 (browser-use as the headless screen server) for correctness, regressions and test coverage.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use, branch release/0.3.2/feat/browser-use. The change is commit cb82345 (review `git diff becf69e cb82345`; the full diff is also at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/browser-use-change.diff). Head b0ba7eb1 only adds a clean merge of the integration branch (a test-file change in bash-atomics).

Requirement: the screen capability's headless form runs `uvx --no-config --default-index https://pypi.org/simple --from browser-use==1.0.0 browser-use --cli-mcp` against a headless Chromium that HolyAgent launches (new `holyagent browser-server` CLI command registered as the Pi MCP server, packages/runtime/src/pi/browser-launch.ts, packages/runtime/src/cli/browser-server.ts) with --remote-debugging-port on a free 127.0.0.1 port and a fresh temporary profile; BU_CDP_URL, ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=0 and temporary state dirs in the server env; cleanup of Chromium and temp dirs on server exit, Chromium exit, signals and failed start; specialists get only mcp__browser_use__browser_exec and mcp__browser_use__browser_screenshot (browser_login off, root excluded); a PyPI pin table (packages/runtime/src/config/pypi-packages.json) moved by deps:update/deps:check via the PyPI JSON API skipping prereleases and yanked releases (scripts/dependency-pins.ts, scripts/update-dependencies.ts); @playwright/mcp removed; the normal form (opencode browse plus pi-computer-use) unchanged; each capability can be turned off.

Writer's own notes to weigh: HOLYAGENT_CHROMIUM_PATH replaces PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH; a SIGKILLed session leaves Chromium and its temp dir behind; UV_INDEX / UV_FIND_LINKS and similar env vars from the person's environment are not scrubbed (only uv config files via --no-config); --no-sandbox is added only when running as root.
constraints: Work only inside /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use; never check out a branch, commit or make any git write in /home/user/holyagent or any other worktree, and make no edits.
Never start pi, uvx, browser-use or a live Chromium, and make no live Kimi, Codex or OpenAI request; unit tests only.
Report blocking findings with file:line and a concrete failure scenario; mark each finding blocking or non-blocking. Report in under 500 words.

result:
result: one blocking finding (signal during Chromium startup leaks Chromium and the temp dir), plus five non-blocking notes. Everything else matches the requirement, and `mise run verify` passes.

built-in /code-review: ran through the Skill tool on `becf69e...cb82345` (effort `medium`) and returned the built-in's own output (six findings, no shadowing seen). I read the cited code for each. One is a blocker (the signal gap) and five are non-blocking.

checks:
- `bunx --no-install mise run verify` in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use, run on head b0ba7eb1 -> exit 0. Type-check (312 files), lint (313 files) and the format check (731 files) are clean. Tests: 3434 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test` on browser-launch, config, tools, setup-browse, setup-chromium, setup-pi, the Pi integration tests, dependency-pins and update-dependencies -> 983 pass, 0 fail.
- Not run, per the constraints: pi, uvx, browser-use, a live Chromium.

blockers:
1. blocking: packages/runtime/src/pi/browser-launch.ts:300-310 and :187-196. A termination signal during startup leaks Chromium and the temp dir.
   - Chromium is spawned `detached`, so it is in its own process group.
   - The signal handlers exist only inside `host.interrupted`, which is raced only after the server has started.
   - Nothing handles SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP during the DevTools poll (up to `READY_TIMEOUT_MS`, 20s) or the server spawn. No `runMain` or signal handler exists elsewhere in runtime src (rg).
   - Scenario: Pi stops the session 1s after launch. Bun's default action ends the launcher with no finalizer, so the `holyagent-browser-*` dir stays and the headless Chromium keeps running. The requirement lists cleanup "on signals".
   - The same happens to a second signal during the up-to-3s grace in `stopGroup`, because `interrupted` removes its handlers once it fires.
   - Tests: the fake `interrupted` in browser-launch.test.ts (the termination-signal test at :232) is only raced after startup, so nothing covers a signal during startup.
   - Repair: install the handlers for the whole run, start of `runBrowserServer` to end of cleanup, for example as an `acquireRelease` at the top that interrupts the main fiber. Add a test that signals while Chromium is still starting and asserts Chromium stop and directory removal.

notes (non-blocking):
- browser-launch.ts:223-224. `stopGroup` returns when `child.exitCode !== null`, so helpers in the group of an already-exited leader are never signalled. On win32 `child.kill()` ends only the top process (the `taskkill /T` fallback runs only after the grace period times out).
- browser-launch.ts:274 `freePort` and :294. The port is probed, released, then Chromium binds it, and `answers` accepts any 2xx on that port. Port 0 plus reading `DevToolsActivePort` from the profile dir would remove the race. It is small and unlikely.
- browser-launch.ts:154-160. The server env names (`BU_CDP_URL`, `BU_NAME`, `BH_HOME`, `BROWSER_HARNESS_HOME`, `BROWSER_USE_CONFIG_DIR`) are asserted only against fakes. I could not confirm that browser-use 1.0.0 `--cli-mcp` reads them (the no-live-run constraint blocks it). Smoke-test the pinned package once.
- chromium.ts:8. `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH` is renamed to `HOLYAGENT_CHROMIUM_PATH` with no fallback, so an old setting is silently ignored. A value in the new variable is never checked for existence, so doctor passes and the failure shows only at launch as `cannot start <path>`.
- Tests for the real host cover the free port, temp dir, DevTools answers and spawn failure. The real `stopGroup` (SIGTERM, then a kill after the grace period) and the real `interrupted` have no test.
- The updater uses the legacy `releases` key of the PyPI JSON API. It works today, but if PyPI drops that key the strict schema fails `deps:update` loudly.
- Writer's own notes: the SIGKILL leak, uv env vars not scrubbed and `--no-sandbox` as root are acceptable as documented. The SIGKILL leak is unavoidable without a pid sweep.
- Checked and fine:
  - The tool allowlist is `browser_exec` and `browser_screenshot` only, and the root excludes `mcp__browser_use__*`.
  - `@playwright/mcp` is removed.
  - The normal form is unchanged, and its `npx` need moved into the normal form.
  - Setup, doctor and the `chromium` need are updated consistently.
  - The updater skips prereleases, post releases and yanked releases, never moves a pin down, and is tested.
  - Cleanup runs in reverse order, and failed starts, no Chromium, no free port and a Chromium that exits early are tested.

There is no test for a signal during startup, nor for the real `stopGroup` or `interrupted`.
- checks-run: `bunx --no-install mise run verify` -> exit 0, 3434 pass / 0 fail. The targeted `bun test` run -> 983 pass / 0 fail.
- findings: the one blocking finding and five non-blocking notes above.
